_about: Commute explainer page (engine/commute/build.py), at docs/toronto/<path>/. Built from Transportation Tomorrow Survey 2022 cross-tabulations exported by hand from the Data Management Group's iDRS (raw/tts/, the files exactly as downloaded): trips into and out of one planning district by start hour and primary mode, and the people who work there by planning district of household (Person table). People present at the end of each hour = the district's residents + all trips in so far - all trips out so far, from 4 a.m. (the survey's day runs 0400-2759). Mode layers net 'in by X' against 'out by X', so they assume people leave the way they came; a layer that dips below zero overnight is drawn at zero. Words in 'page' can use {tokens} that build.py fills from the numbers (see TOKENS in build.py). Boundaries: raw/tts/pd2022.geojson, the 2022 TTS planning districts (simplified to 40 m), joined on PD name with 'aliases' where the iDRS and the shapefile spell a place differently.

page.title: Every weekday, downtown Toronto nearly doubles
page.description: How many people are in downtown Toronto at each hour of an average weekday, how they got there, and where downtown's 677,000 workers live. From the 2022 Transportation Tomorrow Survey.
page.lede: About {residents} people live downtown. By {peakTime} on an average weekday, {peak} people are there: residents plus everyone who came in by subway, GO train, car, bike or on foot. Then it drains. Move the clock to watch it happen.
page.chartNote: Each hour shows the people present when it ends. Residents are counted as home all day unless they made a trip out.
page.howLede: At {peakTime}, almost half of the people who came in rode the TTC. Count every trip in over the whole day, though, and cars bring the most. Drivers come and go; GO riders stay all day.
page.howA: Who's downtown at {peakTime}, by how they arrived
page.howB: Every trip into downtown over the day
page.whereLede: {workers} people have their usual workplace downtown. About one in five lives there too. Two in three live somewhere in Toronto, and one in three commutes from outside the city, some from as far as Owen Sound.
page.whereNote: Shaded by the number of people whose usual workplace is downtown. Tap a district for its count. The survey's planning districts split Toronto into 16 areas; outside Toronto each is a municipality.
page.hybridText: Of downtown's {workers} workers, {commuters} live outside downtown. Yet at the busiest hour, only about {visitors} more people are downtown than at 4 a.m., and that count includes students, shoppers and anyone else who came in. On an average weekday, at least half of downtown's commuters aren't there.
page.hybridSmall: The survey's weekdays lean toward Thursdays and Fridays, when fewer people go in, so a typical Tuesday or Wednesday is likely busier.
method: The numbers come from the 2022 Transportation Tomorrow Survey, a travel survey of about 5% of households across the Greater Golden Horseshoe, taken in fall 2022 and spring 2023 and weighted to the whole population. Each household reported every trip its members aged 5 and up made on one weekday.

Downtown here is the survey's planning district 1: roughly Bathurst Street to the Don River, from the lake to about Bloor Street and the Rosedale ravine, plus Liberty Village, the Exhibition grounds, the Distillery District, the Port Lands and the Toronto Islands.

We start at 4 a.m. with the district's {residents} residents, then add every trip that ended downtown and subtract every trip that left it, hour by hour, by the hour each trip started. Trips that began and ended downtown don't change the count.

What it leaves out: tourists, business travellers and anyone who lives outside the survey area, and children under 5 on their own. So evenings, when visitors matter most, run low. Times are when trips began, so arrivals from far away land a little later than shown. Weekends aren't surveyed.
page.credits: Data: Transportation Tomorrow Survey 2022, Data Management Group, University of Toronto (open data licence). Planning district boundaries: TTS 2022. Analysis and design: Layers.City.
